<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 555eb1ba18c9738e5831b7844822b08fda7c70ac`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 555eb1ba18c9738e5831b7844822b08fda7c70ac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `08d974c5d8317b2edb53f3f78623fd48efcf2d0f` — the merge of head `c15ba57084196643bacd7b42344bb95563a09dcf` into base `555eb1ba18c9738e5831b7844822b08fda7c70ac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 08d974c5d8317b2edb53f3f78623fd48efcf2d0f && git checkout 08d974c5d8317b2edb53f3f78623fd48efcf2d0f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 555eb1ba18c9738e5831b7844822b08fda7c70ac c15ba57084196643bacd7b42344bb95563a09dcf && git checkout -B drift-repro 555eb1ba18c9738e5831b7844822b08fda7c70ac && git merge --no-ff c15ba57084196643bacd7b42344bb95563a09dcf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 555eb1ba18c9738e5831b7844822b08fda7c70ac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 555eb1ba18c9738e5831b7844822b08fda7c70ac` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review for card #30379 · narrowing face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`) · read-only reviewer at the contract-review tier, brief per `record-recognisers --brief-template --face narrowing` · 2026-11-06T05:21Z

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a154e1ba1b6ce5f9552f567b62088bf0e4360e78`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-disable-module-extension-fields.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`withoutWithheldMembers`, `withholdDisabledExtensions`, `resolveObject`, `mergeValidationsByName`, `tenantRuleSettingsOf`, `withPackagedOwnerRules`, `tenantRuleCopyRefusal`), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`referenceTargetOf`), packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-catalog-docs.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, docs/adr/0141-inter-app-dependency-declared-checked-before-install.md (prose read, not reviewed: the changeset, content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx, content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx, content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx)

### ① Derived judgments

- **Placement — right.** The scan runs after the permission check, the catalog wall, the query refusal and the read-only check, and before `registry.disablePackage` and `setPackageDisabled`. It is reads only. The segment from the last `await` through `setPackageDisabled` is synchronous, so no state moves before the refusal.
- **Code and envelope — right.** `409` with the ledgered `PACKAGE_DISABLE_RESTRICTED_BY_VALIDATION_RULE` (PR #30775). There is no `error.details`, per the seat's message-only ruling.
- **Who is scanned — right on the axes ruling A names.**
  - Every severity counts; only `active` is read.
  - Formulas are not refused (the control).
  - Every enabled package counts, declared dependent or not.
  - An app's `.custom` pair is pinned.
  - The read mirrors the validator's `readsRecordColumn` (`record` and `previous`, bare fields, traversals, multi-hop). A hop is judged with `referenceTargetOf`, and the validator fails closed on an undeclared related column.
- **Correctly not refused:**
  - the disabled package's own rule on its own object;
  - a rule of a disabled package, or on an object whose owner is disabled;
  - a rule that reads the field through a formula;
  - a package that is already disabled.
- **Over-refused — WRONG (must-fix 1).** The scan judges every contributor's copy of a rule, but the served fold serves one rule per name.
  - A later layer's copy replaces an earlier one (`mergeValidationsByName`).
  - A tenant overlay sets the packaged rule's `message` and `active` (`tenantRuleSettingsOf` / `withPackagedOwnerRules`). That is a declared capability (ADR-0029 D9.2a), and `tenantRuleCopyRefusal` admits exactly those two keys.

  Three consequences:
  - (a) A packaged extension rule that the tenant switched off through the overlay is still counted. That switch is the only one a tenant admin has on a read-only module. The door then refuses a disable after which no served rule reads the field, and its remedy names a switch that is already thrown.
  - (b) A rule that a later layer replaced by name is still judged from the earlier copy.
  - (c) An overlay seeded from a served read lists the same rule twice.

  None of this is bound by A, and the PR's own contract excludes it.
- **Under-refused — should-fix.** `POST /packages` with `enableOnInstall: false` on an overwrite reaches `registry.disablePackage` with no scan: the same end state by another verb.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/runtime: patch` with the BREAKING banner. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both carriers. One ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). Title `fix(runtime)!:`. Right.
- The docs rows match the code, except that their remedy sentence promises the tenant switch that must-fix 1 does not honour.
- **Must-fix 2.** `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` L7 still says "**57 error codes reachable on the wire**". The PR adds the 58th wire-face heading. `packages/spec/src/api/error-catalog-docs.test.ts` ("the advertised code count matches the wire face") therefore reds **Test Core (2/8)** on this head (`expected 57 to be 58`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Enable door (#30756), cloud disable route (another carrier), the `disableable` verdict (domain:ui card) and the `error.details` contract (a spec card only if needed) are each rightly out of this PR.
- New: the `enableOnInstall: false` overwrite arm (see ①). Fold the same scan in, or file it as its own card.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes ruling A real at the door:
- the refusal sits before any state moves;
- the reader is the platform's one member reader and one reference arbiter;
- the withheld-field reading is the registry's own;
- the message names package · object · rule.

The one exception: in the tenant-overlay state, the door takes away a disable that A permits, and the documented remedy becomes unreachable for the handbook's own audience. That is **must-fix 1**: judge the rules as the fold serves them (one rule per name, the tenant's `active` honoured, attributed to the last contributing layer), with pins for an overlay `active: false` ⇒ 200 and a by-name replacement judged once. **Must-fix 2** is the red required check. Nits: the message says `(no package)` for an overlay rule; `getAllObjects()` is used only to list names.

Check-runs at review time: 32 success, 12 skipped, 1 failure (Test Core 2/8, the catalog count), 4 in progress.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d315efca9756b74d7593a1657229c260b3207e0a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-disable-module-extension-fields.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`withoutWithheldMembers`, `withholdDisabledExtensions`, `resolveObject`, `resolveObjectLeavingExtensionsOut`, `foldExtendersOntoDefinition`, `mergeValidationsByName`, `tenantRuleSettingsOf`, `withPackagedOwnerRules`, `tenantRuleCopyRefusal`, `getAllObjects`, `registerObject`'s priority sort), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`readsRecordColumn`), packages/spec/src/api/error-catalog-docs.test.ts (prose read, not reviewed: the changeset, content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx, content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx, content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx). Judged: the fix commit `d315efca` and the net diff against main (six files); the merge of main `c17719dd` (`356e54ef`) is not reviewed. The head's registry.ts is main's at `c17719dd`; every cited function reads the same there as on the local tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Must-fix 1 (served-fold judging) — CLOSED.** `readDisableDependentRules` now takes each object from `getAllObjects(undefined, { withoutExtensionsOf: id })`, the registry's own fold with this package's `extend` contributions left out, and judges `declaredRulesOf(served)`. Read against the cited code:
  - `resolveObjectLeavingExtensionsOut` keeps the base `overlay ?? own`, folds the kept extenders in the registered (priority-sorted) order and withholds the already-disabled packages' members. So the served list is one rule per name (`mergeValidationsByName`), and a tenant base's copy carries the tenant's `message` and `active` on the packaged rule (`withPackagedOwnerRules` for the owner's rules, `withTenantRuleSettings` inside the merge for an extension's). The scan reads `active === false` off that copy. Honoured.
  - The one step a left-out fold does not take is the disable's own `withoutWithheldMembers` over this package's members. The scan mirrors it: `withheldRules` is every leaving extension's rule name not declared by the owner or a kept extension, exactly `withholdDisabledExtensions`' set once the disable lands, and those names are skipped. `withheldFields` mirrors it the same way (the owner's own fields plus the kept extensions' count as kept; the overlay's copies do not, as in the registry).
  - Attribution: `layerOf` walks the base then the kept `extend` contributions in `getObjectContributors` order, which `registerObject` sorts by priority on every registration, the order `foldExtenders` folds in. Last declaring layer wins, matching the copy the merge serves. `ruleLayerLabel` names an overlay `tenant overlay of PKG` / `tenant overlay`; the `(no package)` placeholder is gone.
  - Break attempts, each read through the fold: an overlay `active: true` over a packaged `active: false` serves the rule on, the scan refuses — right, the write path would run it. An overlay carrying only `message` leaves `active` the package's — judged as served. A later layer's copy that stops reading the field while the earlier copy reads it is not judged (pinned, the override's `qx_credit_not_negative`); the reverse is judged once and named after the later layer (pinned, `qx_credit_review`). A rule of the disabled package itself, carried as a copy on the overlay, is in `withheldRules` and skipped, as the fold will strip it; one that a kept extension also declares is kept by name and judged from the kept copy. A packaged rule the tenant switched off through the overlay no longer refuses, and once every served reader is off the disable answers `200` with the overlay's copies of the fields withheld too (pinned). Nothing found that the served fold would serve and the scan judges differently.
  - Residual nits, not findings: an OWNER rule the tenant copied into the overlay is labelled `tenant overlay of PKG` though its condition is the owner's (the switch lives on the overlay, so the remedy still points right); `declaredFieldNamesOf` filters field values to plain records where the registry's `fieldNamesOf` takes every key, a divergence only on a degenerate body.
- **Must-fix 2 (catalog count) — CLOSED.** `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` L7 reads **58 error codes reachable on the wire**. The head page carries 59 `###` code headings of which two are the one `INVALID_REQUEST` spelling, 58 distinct, one more than before (the new 409 entry). The pin compares the claim with `face.wireCodes.length`; the dev reports `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run test:repo` green at this head (1539/1539). CI's Test Core is still in progress (below).
- **Should-fix (install arm) — ADDRESSED, with a new finding.** `POST /packages` with `enableOnInstall: false` asks the same scan before `disablePackage`; with a reader the row, the registry and the state file all follow `pkg.enabled` (true), and the door answers the same `409` and code with the lead `Package 'ID' was installed and stays enabled`. One pin and one control. Read on ④ below.
- **Placement and envelope — unchanged and right.** The disable door asks the scan after `isDisableablePackage` / `requireWritablePackage` and before `disablePackage` and `setPackageDisabled`; `409` with the ledgered code, no `error.details`; one wire pair for both doors (`check:error-status-conformance` reads it).
- **Over-reach (must-fix 3).** The install arm's scan fires on EVERY `enableOnInstall: false` install, a fresh install included (the arm reads only `request.enableOnInstall`; `overwrite` and the pre-install row are not consulted). On a fresh install of a package whose field an enabled rule already names (a module reinstalled after `DELETE /packages/:id` while a `.custom` rule or another package's rule still reads its field — writes already fail closed there, since #4649), the package lands ENABLED against the caller's explicit `false`, its hooks, flows and navigation live, and the door says it "stays enabled" — it was never enabled. Nothing served is withheld in that case, so ruling A does not reach it, and the ruled install contract (#18877 「有旗 = 设置」: `false ⇒ disablePackage`) is narrowed on a path the PR body and changeset describe only as "an overwrite of an enabled package that asks to come back disabled". Fix: gate the arm on the pre-install row being enabled (the `registry.getPackage(pkgId)` read before the install is at hand), so a fresh install and an overwrite of a disabled package honour `false` as before; and pin a fresh install with a reader answering `201` disabled. Alternatively, if the seat wants the fresh case refused too, the lead, the body, the changeset and the three docs must say so, and the pin must hold it — but that is a narrowing of #18877 beyond A and wants its own ruling.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/runtime: patch` with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset, one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), title `fix(runtime)!:`, model-free trailer pair on the fix commit. Right.
- Body, changeset and docs agree with the code on the served-fold judgment, the layer naming, the overlay's switch as a remedy, and the overwrite case of the install arm. They disagree with the code on the install arm's reach (must-fix 3): the changeset's "The install door too" bullet and the body's install section describe the overwrite case; the catalog, metadata-api and handbook say "the package stays enabled", which is false on the fresh-install path the code also takes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Carried over, rightly out of this PR: the enable door (#30756), the cloud disable route, the `disableable` verdict (domain:ui card), a machine-readable `error.details` (domain:spec card only if the Settings page needs it).
- New: `DELETE /packages/:id` (uninstall) withdraws the same fields with no scan — the same end state by a third verb. Not bound by A; a card, not this PR.
- The fresh-install arm (must-fix 3) is this PR's: it is this diff that adds it.

### ④ Design judgment

- The served-fold scan makes A real exactly where the prior record found it broken: the door now refuses only a disable after which a rule the fold would run reads a withheld field, the tenant's one switch on a read-only module is honoured, and the message names the layer the admin must act on. The reader stays the platform's one member reader and reference arbiter, the fold is the registry's own, not a second copy. Five ablations each red, including the per-copy reading the prior record measured.
- The install arm's `409` after a landed write, judged against the door's contract and the docs: on an overwrite of an enabled package it is coherent. The end state is what a plain overwrite leaves, nothing goes live that was not live, only the disable half is refused, the lead sentence says what landed, the catalog's entry names both doors, and a pin holds the row, the state file and the served field. The remaining tension — one code meaning "nothing changed" on one door and "the install landed" on the other — is carried by the lead and the catalog text, and `no_retry` fits. Undoing the install would be a second write the request did not ask for; refusing before the install would need the scan asked of an artifact not yet registered. Acceptable as documented. On a fresh install it is a half-state the docs do not describe and the ruling does not cover: must-fix 3.

Check-runs at review time on `d315efca`: 19 success, 14 skipped, 18 in progress (Test Core 1–8, Build Core, Build Docs, the Lint and Type Check lanes, Check Changeset), 0 failure. The gate verdicts are not yet in.
